title: Monarch Money Alternatives 2026: Plans and Prices
h1: Monarch Money Alternatives 2026: Plans and Prices
metaDescription: Compare Monarch Money alternatives: YNAB, Copilot Money, Quicken Simplifi, PocketGuard, Tiller and Goodbudget, with regular plan prices and trials.
intro:
YNAB, Copilot Money, Quicken Simplifi, PocketGuard, Tiller and Goodbudget are six Monarch Money alternatives, with regular entry prices ranging from a $0 free plan to $109 per year. At The Modern Wallet, we calculate the yearly expense of budgeting subscriptions so households can see what monthly rates, annual commitments and lifetime options cost over time.

[Monarch Money](https://www.monarchmoney.com/pricing) sells two subscription tiers: Core at $99.99 per year or $14.99 per month, and Plus at $199.99 per year. Monarch Money lists a free first week under the phrase "Your first week is on us" and provides a no-questions-asked money-back guarantee with permission to cancel anytime. Monarch Money notes that it displays no ads, states that it never sells financial data, and maintains a 4.9 rating across more than 100,000 reviews as stated on its pricing page. Monarch Money recommends completing sign-up on the web rather than through the Apple App Store or Google Play.

For readers who want a broader overview of personal finance software, our [best budgeting apps roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps/) tracks wider category options. Partners managing money together can examine the [best budgeting apps for couples roundup](/roundup/best-budgeting-apps-for-couples/), and planners establishing spending categories can review our [guide on how to make a budget](/guides/how-to-make-a-budget/).

chooseSection.heading: How to Choose a Monarch Money Alternative
chooseSection.body:
Selecting a replacement for Monarch Money begins with five operational factors: the billing commitment, the length of the evaluation trial, the method of connecting financial accounts, the underlying budgeting model, and whether an application interface or a spreadsheet fits daily tracking habits.

First, assess the billing commitment. Monarch Money Core charges $99.99 on an annual basis or $14.99 on a month-to-month schedule. Paying month to month for 12 months totals $179.88, which is an $79.89 premium over the single annual payment. YNAB charges $109 annually or $14.99 monthly, yielding the same $179.88 annual total on monthly billing. PocketGuard offers an annual tier at $74.99, a monthly rate at $12.99 (which totals $155.88 over 12 months), and a permanent Lifetime purchase at $149.99. Tiller avoids monthly subscriptions entirely by charging $99 per year. Goodbudget provides a $0 tier alongside an $80 annual plan or a $10 monthly rate ($120 per year).

Second, evaluate the free trial terms. Monarch Money lists a 7-day free trial under the phrase "Your first week is on us." PocketGuard also uses a 7-day trial across its plans. In contrast, YNAB offers a 34-day free trial that requires no credit card details at registration, meaning no charge occurs unless the user chooses to subscribe. Tiller grants a 30-day trial without charging the card until the period concludes, paired with a subsequent 30-day refund window that offers up to 60 days of risk-free evaluation. Copilot Money and Quicken Simplifi list no specific free trial days on their pricing pages.

Third, review bank connectivity and platforms. Quicken Simplifi connects to 14,000+ financial institutions, while Copilot Money connects to 16,000+ banks. Tiller pulls transaction data automatically into personal spreadsheets. Goodbudget restricts automatic bank synchronization to United States (US) banks on its Premium tier. Copilot Money supports iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Web, whereas Goodbudget supports Web, Android, and iPhone.

Fourth, determine the budgeting methodology. Monarch Money utilizes general expense categorizing, forecasting, and investment monitoring. Users can test zero-allocation math using our [zero-based budget calculator](/budget/zero-based-budget-calculator/). Quicken Simplifi organizes spending through a custom Spending Plan and projects cash flow 12 months into the future. Goodbudget enforces digital envelope budgeting, allocating specific balances to fixed categories. 

Finally, decide between a standalone application and a spreadsheet. Applications like Copilot Money and Goodbudget provide mobile app interfaces. 

Who this is not for:
- People who require completely offline bookkeeping with paper receipts or locally hosted desktop files.
- Businesses needing specialized enterprise enterprise payroll, double-entry ledgers, and formal client invoicing.
- Anyone who does not want to connect banking credentials or manually record personal transactions.

What would change our answer:
- Monarch Money altering its $99.99 Core or $199.99 Plus prices, or eliminating its 7-day trial.
- YNAB shifting its 34-day no-card trial policy or adjusting its $109 annual list price.
- Copilot Money publishing a permanent monthly plan price or officially launching its multi-user household system.
- PocketGuard removing its $149.99 one-time Lifetime option.

alternatives.heading: YNAB Pricing and Budgeting System Compared with Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
YNAB is a personal budgeting application with annual and monthly subscription options. The company publishes two standard plans: an Annual plan at $109 USD paid annually (which equals $9.08 per month) and a Monthly plan at $14.99 per month, plus applicable sales tax. YNAB includes a 34-day free trial that requires no credit card to start, guaranteeing that users are never billed unless they manually subscribe.

YNAB fits people who want an extended 34-day trial without entering a credit card. 

YNAB falls short of Monarch Money for users seeking multi-income forecasting and integrated investment analysis. Monarch Money Plus includes tools to track diverse income streams such as small businesses, along with forecasting tools and deeper investment tracking. Furthermore, Monarch Money offers an active For Couples page with household sharing.

On annual subscription costs, YNAB at $109 per year costs $9.01 more than Monarch Money Core at $99.99 per year. On monthly billing, both products charge $14.99 per month, which totals $179.88 across 12 billing cycles. Over five years on annual billing, YNAB totals $545.00, while Monarch Money Core totals $499.95, establishing a five-year difference of $45.05.

alternatives.heading: Copilot Money Features and Apple Focus Versus Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
Copilot Money is an account tracking and personal finance application available on iPhone, iPad, Mac, and Web. Its pricing page lists an annual subscription at $109 per year, which equates to $9 per month, labeled as a limited-time offer discounted from its standard $119 price. Copilot Money specifies that it has no tiers, no add-ons, and no artificial intelligence (AI) credits, while providing support from real humans and connectivity to 16,000+ banks. Monthly subscription pricing is not published on the page.

Copilot Money fits Mac, iPhone, iPad, and Web users who want a money assistant across their devices.

Copilot Money falls short of Monarch Money on cross-platform accessibility and shared household access. Copilot Money states on its page that inviting a partner is "coming this fall" under a Households feature, whereas Monarch Money maintains a For Couples page with household sharing. 

Comparing published annual commitments, Copilot Money at its $109 promotional price costs $9.01 more per year than Monarch Money Core at $99.99. If Copilot Money returns to its regular $119 price, the difference expands to $19.01 per year. Monarch Money Plus at $199.99 per year sits $90.99 above Copilot Money's $109 tier. Because Copilot Money does not display a monthly billing option, budgeters wanting monthly flexibility cannot compare month-to-month spending directly.

alternatives.heading: Quicken Simplifi Cash Flow Projections Compared with Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
Quicken Simplifi is a personal finance tool accessible on mobile devices and the web. The service connects to 14,000+ financial institutions to automatically monitor accounts, track net worth, and organize a dynamic Spending Plan. It includes Projected Cash Flow modeling extending up to 12 months ahead, alongside free one-on-one setup help from Quicken experts. Quicken Simplifi displays a regular list price of $6.99 per month billed annually, accompanied by a promotional offer of $3.99 per month billed annually.

Quicken Simplifi fits individuals who prioritize forward-looking cash flow projections and who want expert onboarding assistance to configure their spending categories.

Quicken Simplifi falls short of Monarch Money in deeper investment tracking and partner sharing. Monarch Money Plus provides specialized tracking for multiple revenue sources like a small business, along with deeper investment tracking. Quicken Simplifi also lacks a published standalone monthly billing option on its product page.

Evaluating annual costs without promotional rates, Quicken Simplifi at its regular $6.99 per month billed annually costs $83.88 per year (12 x $6.99). Monarch Money Core costs $99.99 per year. Quicken Simplifi's regular price saves $16.11 per year compared with Monarch Money Core. When compared with Monarch Money Plus at $199.99 per year, Quicken Simplifi's regular tier saves $116.11 annually.

alternatives.heading: PocketGuard Plans and Lifetime Access Versus Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
PocketGuard is a personal budgeting application with monthly, annual, and lifetime plan options. Its pricing page lists Premium Yearly at $74.99 billed annually (equating to $6.25 per month, advertised with a "Save $81/year" callout), Monthly billing at $12.99 per month, and a Lifetime option for a one-time payment of $149.99. PocketGuard provides a 7-day free trial on all options, accompanied by priority human customer support and AI chat assistance.

PocketGuard fits budgeters who want an annual plan or who prefer paying a single one-time fee to eliminate ongoing subscription expenses.

PocketGuard falls short of Monarch Money for partner sharing and multi-income tracking. Monarch Money delivers deeper investment tracking, a For Couples page, and small-business income tracking on Plus. 

From a cost perspective, PocketGuard Premium Yearly at $74.99 per year saves $25.00 annually compared to Monarch Money Core at $99.99. On monthly billing, PocketGuard charges $12.99 per month ($155.88 over 12 months), whereas Monarch Money Core charges $14.99 per month ($179.88 over 12 months), a yearly difference of $24.00. Most notably, PocketGuard Lifetime costs $149.99 once. Two years of Monarch Money Core costs $199.98 (2 x $99.99), meaning PocketGuard Lifetime costs $49.99 less than 24 months of Monarch Money Core.

alternatives.heading: Tiller Spreadsheet Automation Compared with Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
Tiller is a financial service that puts account data into spreadsheets automatically. Tiller charges $99 per year, plus sales tax where required, with no advertisements or hidden fees. The service begins with a 30-day free trial where payment cards are not charged until the trial concludes, followed by an additional 30-day full refund guarantee, creating up to 60 days of risk-free testing. Tiller exports financial data into Google Sheets and Microsoft Excel templates.

Tiller fits spreadsheet enthusiasts who want account data placed into spreadsheets automatically.

Tiller falls short of Monarch Money for users who prefer an application interface rather than spreadsheets. 

On annual subscription pricing, Tiller costs $99.00 per year, which is virtually identical to Monarch Money Core at $99.99 per year, presenting a negligible difference of $0.99 annually. Over three years, Tiller costs $297.00 while Monarch Money Core totals $299.97. However, Tiller does not offer a month-to-month billing plan, whereas Monarch Money Core allows users to pay $14.99 monthly.

alternatives.heading: Goodbudget Envelope Budgeting and Free Tier Versus Monarch Money
alternatives.body:
Goodbudget is an envelope budgeting platform available on the Web, Android, and iPhone. Its pricing page features a Free plan at $0 that includes 10 regular envelopes, 10 more envelopes, 1 account, 2 devices, 1 year of historical records, debt tracking, and community support. Goodbudget Premium costs $10 per month or $80 per year, expanding features to automatic bank synchronization for US institutions, unlimited envelopes, unlimited accounts, 5 devices, 7 years of transaction history, and direct email support.

Goodbudget fits planners who want envelope budgeting and who prefer starting on a $0 plan before paying for software.

Goodbudget falls short of Monarch Money in comprehensive asset tracking and modern account synchronization. Goodbudget Free restricts users to a single account and omits automatic bank sync. Even Goodbudget Premium limits automated sync to US banks and omits deeper investment tracking, forecasting tools, and small business revenue tracking.

Comparing financial plans, Goodbudget Free costs $0, providing an annual savings of $99.99 compared to Monarch Money Core and $199.99 compared to Monarch Money Plus. Goodbudget Premium at $80 per year billed annually saves $19.99 per year relative to Monarch Money Core. On monthly schedules, Goodbudget Premium at $10 per month costs $120.00 annually, which is $59.88 less than Monarch Money Core's $179.88 annual total on monthly billing.

stillBetterFit.heading: When Monarch Money Is Still the Better Fit
stillBetterFit.body:
Monarch Money Core provides household sharing and partner collaboration without ads.

For households managing multiple revenue streams, Monarch Money Plus at $199.99 per year introduces dedicated forecasting tools, small-business income tracking, and deeper investment tracking. These capabilities sit beyond envelope tools like Goodbudget or subscriptions like YNAB. Monarch Money also emphasizes user privacy by operating without advertisements and stating explicitly that it never sells customer financial data.

Monarch Money accommodates users who prefer flexibility by supporting monthly billing at $14.99 alongside its $99.99 annual Core rate. New subscribers receive a free first week under the "Your first week is on us" trial and access to a no-questions-asked money-back guarantee.

verdict:
Monarch Money Core costs $99.99 per year, while alternatives range from Goodbudget's $0 Free tier to YNAB and Copilot Money at $109 per year. Quicken Simplifi offers a lower annual regular list price of $83.88 ($6.99 per month), PocketGuard provides budgeters an annual rate of $74.99 and a permanent Lifetime purchase at $149.99, and Tiller matches Monarch Money almost dollar for dollar at $99 per year for automated spreadsheet feeds.

To pick the best alternative for your finances, identify whether you require envelope allocations, spreadsheet freedom, or shared household visibility, and compare the published rates in our table above. You can explore broader personal finance tool comparisons across our site in our [financial product comparison hub](/compare/).

faqs.question: Is there a free alternative to Monarch Money?
faqs.answer: Yes. Goodbudget provides a Free plan at $0 per month. The free tier includes 10 regular envelopes, 10 more envelopes, 1 account, 2 devices, 1 year of history, debt tracking, and community support. Goodbudget Free does not include automatic bank synchronization.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest Monarch Money alternative?
faqs.answer: Goodbudget Free is the cheapest ongoing alternative at $0. Among paid annual subscriptions, Quicken Simplifi lists a regular price of $6.99 per month billed annually ($83.88 per year), and PocketGuard lists Premium Yearly at $74.99 per year ($6.25 per month). PocketGuard also offers a one-time Lifetime plan for $149.99.

faqs.question: Does Monarch Money have a free trial?
faqs.answer: Yes. Monarch Money includes a 7-day free trial on its pricing page with the phrase "Your first week is on us." Monarch Money also provides a no-questions-asked money-back guarantee and allows users to cancel at any time.

faqs.question: How does Monarch Money pricing compare to YNAB?
faqs.answer: Monarch Money Core costs $99.99 per year, which is $9.01 lower than YNAB's $109 annual subscription. On monthly billing, both Monarch Money Core and YNAB charge $14.99 per month, which totals $179.88 over 12 months. YNAB offers a 34-day free trial with no credit card required, while Monarch Money offers a 7-day trial.

faqs.question: Which alternative is closest to Monarch for couples?
faqs.answer: Monarch Money includes built-in partner sharing and maintains a dedicated For Couples page. Among alternatives, Copilot Money states on its pricing page that inviting a partner is "coming this fall" under a Households feature, but the feature is not yet available.
